findings.first_failure: Commit 799793a (2026-08-30, by Ron: "two Stop hooks demanded a record of work that never happened") added a module-level _in_repo() helper to chain-gate.py to fix a real unanchored-path bug, but appended the new def after the file's existing `if __name__ == "__main__": raise SystemExit(main())`. main() calls _in_repo() whenever the transcript shows a chains write, so every such Stop run since that commit raises NameError.
findings.diagnosis: Verified by parsing all 7 hook files with ast: only chain-gate.py and radar-gate.py define a function after their __main__ guard; the other five define every helper first. A minimal repro (main() calling a name defined later in the same file) reproduces the identical NameError at exit code 1. The 5 tests this same commit added (test_pressure.py) import the hook via importlib.exec_module, so __name__ is never "__main__" there and main() never runs, which is why the suite never saw this.
findings.smallest_change: Move `def _in_repo(...)` (the last ~35 lines of the file) to above `if __name__ == "__main__":` in chain-gate.py and radar-gate.py. Pure reorder, no logic change. Verify with a real subprocess invocation (python3 <hook> < payload), the way Claude Code actually runs it, not only importlib import: import-based tests pass either way because they never set __name__ to "__main__".
findings.regression_case: A subprocess-based case, mirroring test_campaign_hooks.py's [sys.executable, HOOKS/f'{name}-gate.py'] pattern (used today for campaign, universe and profile but not chain or radar), piping a synthetic transcript with a chains write into chain-gate.py fails today with NameError: name '_in_repo' is not defined, exit code 1.
